englishTranslation: to resume / to pick up again / to recover / to retake
grammarNotes: Riprendere is a compound verb formed from ri- (again) + prendere (to take), and it follows the same irregular conjugation as prendere in all tenses. In compound tenses it takes avere as its auxiliary: ho ripreso, avevo ripreso. The past participle is ripreso — irregular, like preso. In the future tense (riprenderà, riprenderemo) it expresses a scheduled or anticipated resumption of activity, making it the standard verb in announcements and formal contexts: 'I lavori riprenderanno lunedì' (Work will resume Monday). When used reflexively as riprendersi, it shifts meaning to 'to recover' from illness or shock.
learnerNotes: English speakers often reach for ricominciare when they mean riprendere, but the two are not interchangeable. Ricominciare means to start over from the beginning; riprendere means to pick up where you left off — the distinction matters. Think of a film after an interval: it riprende, it doesn't ricomincia. The ri- prefix is the key: it signals resumption, not fresh start. Also worth memorizing: 'riprendere fiato' (to catch one's breath) and 'riprendersi dal jet lag' (to recover from jet lag) — both common and natural.

exampleSentences.italian: La riunione riprende tra cinque minuti.
exampleSentences.english: The meeting resumes in five minutes.

exampleSentences.italian: Dopo le vacanze, ho ripreso il lavoro con più energia.
exampleSentences.english: After the holidays, I picked up work again with more energy.

exampleSentences.italian: I treni riprenderanno a circolare domani mattina.
exampleSentences.english: Trains will resume running tomorrow morning.

exampleSentences.italian: Si è ripresa bene dall'operazione.
exampleSentences.english: She recovered well from the operation.

exampleSentences.italian: Riprendiamo da dove eravamo rimasti.
exampleSentences.english: Let's pick up from where we left off.

relatedExpressions.meaning: to recover (from illness, shock, or difficulty)
to catch one's breath
to regain consciousness / to come to

grammarNotes: Arrivo is a masculine noun (l'arrivo, gli arrivi). It is formed from the verb arrivare and functions as both a standalone noun and — crucially — as part of a fixed prepositional phrase. The construction all'arrivo (al + arrivo, contracted to all' before a vowel) means 'upon arrival' or 'on arrival' and is extremely common in transport, hospitality, and formal announcements. The apostrophe in all' is not optional — it signals elision of the article before a vowel and is always written.
learnerNotes: The phrase all'arrivo is one of a productive family of constructions using al/alla/all' + noun that describe the moment of reaching a destination or threshold: all'arrivo, alla partenza, all'uscita, all'ingresso. Mastering this pattern unlocks natural-sounding Italian in airports, train stations, hotels, and events. Note that arrivo also means 'finish line' in sports — 'tagliare il traguardo all'arrivo' — so context matters. In everyday speech, 'sono in arrivo' (I'm on my way / I'm nearly there) is a very common and useful expression.

exampleSentences.italian: All'arrivo, ti aspetto fuori dall'aeroporto.
exampleSentences.english: On arrival, I'll wait for you outside the airport.

exampleSentences.italian: Il treno è in arrivo al binario tre.
exampleSentences.english: The train is arriving at platform three.

exampleSentences.italian: All'arrivo in hotel, ci hanno offerto un drink di benvenuto.
exampleSentences.english: On arrival at the hotel, they offered us a welcome drink.

exampleSentences.italian: Gli arrivi internazionali sono al terminal B.
exampleSentences.english: International arrivals are at terminal B.

relatedExpressions.meaning: upon arrival / on arrival
to be on the way / to be arriving
arrival time / estimated time of arrival

grammarNotes: Partenza is a feminine noun (la partenza, le partenze), derived from the verb partire. Like arrivo, it pairs naturally with the preposition a to form alla partenza (at/upon departure). The construction follows the same logic as all'arrivo: al/alla/all' + noun signals the moment of a transition. In transport contexts, 'le partenze' (departures) is the plural form you'll see on departure boards. Partenza is also used in sports and racing to mean 'start' — la partenza is the noun for the starting event itself.
learnerNotes: Alla partenza pairs naturally with all'arrivo as its mirror — if you know one, you know the other. A useful real-world phrase is 'in partenza' (departing / about to leave): 'Il treno in partenza dal binario uno' is what you'll hear over the PA system at every Italian train station. Notice that 'in partenza' and 'in arrivo' are the two most common transport announcements in Italian — internalising them makes navigating stations and airports dramatically easier. Punto di partenza (starting point) is also widely used figuratively in discussions and presentations.

exampleSentences.italian: Alla partenza, ci siamo salutati con un abbraccio.
exampleSentences.english: At departure, we said goodbye with a hug.

exampleSentences.italian: Il volo in partenza per Roma è in ritardo.
exampleSentences.english: The departing flight to Rome is delayed.

exampleSentences.italian: Le partenze sono al piano superiore.
exampleSentences.english: Departures are on the upper floor.

exampleSentences.italian: Alla partenza dei corridori, la folla ha applaudito.
exampleSentences.english: At the start of the runners, the crowd applauded.

relatedExpressions.meaning: at departure / upon departure
departing / about to leave
starting point / point of departure

grammarNotes: Uscita is a feminine noun (l'uscita, le uscite), derived from the verb uscire. The prepositional phrase all'uscita (all' + uscita, with elision before the vowel) means 'at the exit' or 'upon leaving.' Beyond the transport and physical-space sense, uscita also means an outing or casual trip — 'una uscita con gli amici' (an outing with friends) — and in formal Italian it can refer to an outgoing payment or expenditure. The plural le uscite covers all these senses depending on context.
learnerNotes: All'uscita is the third member of the al/alla/all' family alongside all'arrivo and alla partenza, but it has an extra dimension: it refers to a specific point in space (the exit) as much as a moment in time (upon leaving). You'll hear 'ci vediamo all'uscita' (see you at the exit / see you when we come out) constantly — after school, after a concert, after the cinema. The informal sense of uscita covering casual plans surprises learners: 'facciamo un'uscita?' means 'shall we go out?' — a very natural everyday usage.

exampleSentences.italian: Ci vediamo all'uscita del cinema.
exampleSentences.english: See you at the exit of the cinema.

exampleSentences.italian: All'uscita dalla metropolitana, gira a destra.
exampleSentences.english: On leaving the metro, turn right.

exampleSentences.italian: L'uscita di emergenza è in fondo al corridoio.
exampleSentences.english: The emergency exit is at the end of the corridor.

exampleSentences.italian: Abbiamo organizzato un'uscita in barca per sabato.
exampleSentences.english: We've organised a boat outing for Saturday.

relatedExpressions.meaning: at the exit / upon leaving
emergency exit
to go on an outing / to go out casually

grammarNotes: Ingresso is a masculine noun (l'ingresso, gli ingressi), derived via Latin ingressus. The prepositional phrase all'ingresso means 'at the entrance' or 'upon entry.' Ingresso also carries the sense of admission — 'ingresso libero' (free entry) and 'ingresso a pagamento' (paid admission) are standard signs at museums, exhibitions, and events. Unlike uscita, which has the extra informal sense of an outing, ingresso stays firmly in the spatial and institutional domain.
learnerNotes: All'ingresso completes the four-part family: all'arrivo, alla partenza, all'uscita, all'ingresso. Of the four, ingresso is the most formal in register — you're more likely to see it on signage and in announcements than in casual speech, where 'all'entrata' is sometimes used instead. Practically: 'ingresso libero' on a museum or gallery sign means no ticket required — a phrase worth knowing immediately. Ingresso can also refer to the entrance hall of a home: 'aspettami nell'ingresso' means 'wait for me in the entrance hall' — a domestic usage learners often miss.

exampleSentences.italian: All'ingresso del museo, bisogna mostrare il biglietto.
exampleSentences.english: At the entrance to the museum, you need to show your ticket.

exampleSentences.italian: L'ingresso è gratuito per i bambini sotto i dodici anni.
exampleSentences.english: Entry is free for children under twelve.

exampleSentences.italian: All'ingresso della villa c'è un cancello in ferro battuto.
exampleSentences.english: At the entrance to the villa there is a wrought-iron gate.

exampleSentences.italian: Lascia le scarpe nell'ingresso, per favore.
exampleSentences.english: Leave your shoes in the entrance hall, please.

relatedExpressions.meaning: at the entrance / upon entry
free entry / free admission
no entry / entry forbidden

grammarNotes: Decisamente is an adverb formed from the adjective deciso (decided, firm) via the standard Italian adverb construction: feminine singular adjective + -mente. It is invariable — it never agrees with gender or number. Decisamente typically modifies adjectives ('decisamente migliore' — decidedly better), verbs ('ha decisamente rifiutato' — she flatly refused), or entire clauses when placed at the start for emphasis. Its position is flexible: it can open a sentence, follow the verb, or precede the adjective it modifies.
learnerNotes: Decisamente is stronger and more emphatic than semplicemente or abbastanza — it carries a confident 'no doubt about it' quality. Learners sometimes confuse it with sicuramente (surely, certainly) or assolutamente (absolutely), but decisamente has a sharper, more opinionated edge — it expresses a judgment, not just certainty. In spoken Italian it functions well as a standalone response: 'decisamente!' means 'absolutely!' or 'no question!' A practical tip: if you're tempted to say 'molto' + adjective for emphasis, consider whether decisamente would sound more natural and grown-up.

exampleSentences.italian: Questo ristorante è decisamente migliore dell'altro.
exampleSentences.english: This restaurant is decidedly better than the other one.

exampleSentences.italian: Ha decisamente rifiutato l'offerta senza pensarci.
exampleSentences.english: She flatly refused the offer without thinking about it.

exampleSentences.italian: Decisamente, avremmo dovuto prenotare prima.
exampleSentences.english: We definitely should have booked earlier.

exampleSentences.italian: Il film era decisamente troppo lungo.
exampleSentences.english: The film was decidedly too long.

relatedExpressions.meaning: absolutely — stronger and more absolute in tone
surely / certainly — about probability rather than emphasis
clearly — factual rather than emphatic

englishTranslation: thoroughly / in depth / to the bottom
grammarNotes: A fondo is an adverbial phrase — it functions as an adverb modifying a verb and is always written as two words (never afondo). It most commonly follows the verb it modifies: 'studiare a fondo' (to study thoroughly), 'esaminare a fondo' (to examine in depth), 'conoscere a fondo' (to know thoroughly). The literal meaning is 'to the bottom,' which gives the idiomatic sense of going all the way down into something — comprehensive, without leaving anything unexplored. It cannot be used before a noun; it is strictly adverbial.
learnerNotes: A fondo pairs most naturally with verbs of mental effort and investigation: studiare, esaminare, analizzare, conoscere, capire, approfondire. It's the phrase to reach for when you want to say you've done something with genuine depth rather than superficially. A common pitfall: learners sometimes use completamente or totalmente instead, but those convey completion or totality, not depth. 'Ho studiato completamente il capitolo' means I finished the chapter; 'ho studiato a fondo il capitolo' means I really worked through it carefully — a meaningful difference.

exampleSentences.italian: Bisogna studiare a fondo la grammatica italiana.
exampleSentences.english: You need to study Italian grammar thoroughly.

exampleSentences.italian: I medici hanno esaminato il paziente a fondo prima di decidere.
exampleSentences.english: The doctors examined the patient thoroughly before deciding.

exampleSentences.italian: Non conosco a fondo la cultura giapponese, ma mi affascina.
exampleSentences.english: I don't know Japanese culture in depth, but it fascinates me.

exampleSentences.italian: Dobbiamo analizzare a fondo le cause del problema.
exampleSentences.english: We need to analyse the causes of the problem in depth.

relatedExpressions.meaning: to go deeper into / to explore in depth — the verb equivalent of a fondo
in detail — focuses on specifics rather than overall depth
in a thorough manner — more formal synonym

grammarNotes: Tenebre is a feminine plural noun — it has no singular form in standard Italian usage (it is plurale tantum). You say 'le tenebre' always, never 'la tenebra' in ordinary usage (though 'la tenebra' occasionally appears in poetry). It takes plural agreement throughout: 'le tenebre erano fitte' (the darkness was thick), 'queste tenebre pesanti' (this heavy gloom). Because it is always plural, it pairs with plural adjectives and plural verbs, even when English treats the concept as singular.
learnerNotes: Italian has three main words for darkness — buio, oscurità, and tenebre — and choosing the right one matters. Buio is the everyday word: concrete, neutral, used whenever the lights are off or a room is dark ('ho paura del buio' — I'm afraid of the dark). Oscurità is more formal and abstract, often found in scientific or descriptive writing. Tenebre belongs to the literary and figurative register — religious texts, poetry, dramatic narrative, and metaphor. It implies not just absence of light but a quality of menace, mystery, or moral weight — the darkness of evil, of the soul, of the unknown. You would never say 'ho paura delle tenebre' in casual speech; that's a poetic statement, not an everyday complaint.

exampleSentences.italian: Il castello era avvolto nelle tenebre della notte.
exampleSentences.english: The castle was wrapped in the darkness of the night.

exampleSentences.italian: La luce vinse sulle tenebre.
exampleSentences.english: Light triumphed over darkness.

exampleSentences.italian: Viveva nelle tenebre dell'ignoranza.
exampleSentences.english: He lived in the darkness of ignorance.

exampleSentences.italian: Le tenebre scesero sulla città dopo il tramonto.
exampleSentences.english: Darkness fell over the city after sunset.

relatedExpressions.meaning: darkness — everyday, neutral, concrete (lights off, a dark room)
darkness / obscurity — formal and descriptive, less metaphorical than tenebre
prince of darkness — fixed phrase for the devil

englishTranslation: to leave / to go away / to be off
grammarNotes: Andarsene is a pronominal verb — andare combined with the reflexive particle si and the partitive particle ne, fused together. In conjugation, si becomes the reflexive pronoun matching the subject (me ne vado, te ne vai, se ne va, ce ne andiamo, ve ne andate, se ne vanno), and ne remains in place. In compound tenses it takes essere as its auxiliary, and the past participle andato agrees with the subject in gender and number: 'me ne sono andato' (masculine), 'me ne sono andata' (feminine). This agreement rule is the most common error learners make with this verb.
learnerNotes: Andarsene is not simply a synonym for andare. The particle ne adds a sense of definitive departure — leaving a place entirely, often with a nuance of finality, relief, or drama that plain andare lacks. 'Vado' means I'm going (somewhere); 'me ne vado' means I'm leaving (this place, getting out of here). The register ranges from calm to emphatic depending on context and tone — the same phrase can signal a polite exit or a dramatic storming-out. The imperative 'vattene!' (go away! / get out!) is extremely common and impossible to understand without knowing this construction, so it's worth memorising early.

exampleSentences.italian: È tardi, me ne vado.
exampleSentences.english: It's late, I'm off.

exampleSentences.italian: Se ne è andato senza salutare nessuno.
exampleSentences.english: He left without saying goodbye to anyone.

exampleSentences.italian: Dopo la discussione, ce ne siamo andati in silenzio.
exampleSentences.english: After the argument, we left in silence.

exampleSentences.italian: Vattene! Non voglio vederti.
exampleSentences.english: Go away! I don't want to see you.

exampleSentences.italian: Me ne sono andato prima della fine dello spettacolo.
exampleSentences.english: I left before the end of the show.

relatedExpressions.meaning: go away! / get out! — imperative, very common in spoken Italian
to make off / to get away — more colloquial, often implies urgency or escape
to get out of the way / to remove oneself — emphatic, often figurative

grammarNotes: Intelligenza artificiale is a feminine noun phrase: l'intelligenza artificiale, abbreviated as IA. The abbreviation follows Italian word order — intelligenza first, artificiale second — which is why the Italian acronym is IA and not AI. In Italian texts and speech, both the full form and the abbreviation are common; IA is increasingly used in headlines and casual reference. The phrase takes feminine agreement throughout: 'l'IA è diventata potente' (AI has become powerful), 'le intelligenze artificiali' (artificial intelligences, plural). When used as a modifier it remains invariable: 'un sistema di IA', 'strumenti di intelligenza artificiale'.
learnerNotes: The single most important thing to know: Italians say and write IA, not AI. If you say 'AI' with the English pronunciation in an Italian conversation, you will be understood — it's creeping into usage — but IA is the correct and standard Italian form, and using it marks you as someone who knows the language well. The full phrase intelligenza artificiale is formal and appears in journalism, academia, and official discourse; in casual conversation Italians increasingly just say 'la IA' or even borrow 'l'AI' (pronounced as two letters). Either way, the article is always feminine: la IA, l'IA.

exampleSentences.italian: L'intelligenza artificiale sta cambiando il mondo del lavoro.
exampleSentences.english: Artificial intelligence is changing the world of work.

exampleSentences.italian: Il governo ha presentato nuove norme sull'uso della IA.
exampleSentences.english: The government has introduced new rules on the use of AI.

exampleSentences.italian: Molte aziende italiane stanno investendo nell'intelligenza artificiale.
exampleSentences.english: Many Italian companies are investing in artificial intelligence.

exampleSentences.italian: La IA generativa è al centro del dibattito pubblico.
exampleSentences.english: Generative AI is at the centre of public debate.

exampleSentences.italian: Non capisco ancora bene come funziona l'intelligenza artificiale.
exampleSentences.english: I still don't fully understand how artificial intelligence works.

relatedExpressions.meaning: generative AI — the specific term for systems like large language models
applied AI — AI used in specific practical domains
AI ethics — a growing field of public and academic discussion

grammarNotes: Algoritmo is a masculine noun (l'algoritmo, gli algoritmi). It entered Italian from medieval Latin via Arabic — the word derives from the name of the 9th-century mathematician al-Khwarizmi. In contemporary usage it appears both in precise technical contexts and in loose everyday speech, where it often means simply 'the system that decides what I see online.' The plural gli algoritmi is standard; in journalism you'll frequently see 'gli algoritmi dei social media' (social media algorithms) and 'l'algoritmo di raccomandazione' (recommendation algorithm).
learnerNotes: Algoritmo has crossed from technical jargon into everyday Italian conversation, particularly around social media and online platforms. Italians now routinely say things like 'l'algoritmo mi ha consigliato questo video' (the algorithm recommended this video to me) or 'devo capire come funziona l'algoritmo' (I need to understand how the algorithm works) in perfectly casual speech. The stress falls on the second syllable: al-GO-rit-mo — a common mispronunciation among English speakers who stress the first syllable as in English. Getting the stress right makes a real difference to naturalness.

exampleSentences.italian: L'algoritmo di Instagram decide quali post vedere per primo.
exampleSentences.english: Instagram's algorithm decides which posts you see first.

exampleSentences.italian: Gli esperti hanno analizzato l'algoritmo per trovare eventuali bias.
exampleSentences.english: Experts analysed the algorithm to find any biases.

exampleSentences.italian: Non so come funziona l'algoritmo, ma sembra che sappia tutto di me.
exampleSentences.english: I don't know how the algorithm works, but it seems to know everything about me.

exampleSentences.italian: Molti algoritmi di IA vengono addestrati su enormi quantità di dati.
exampleSentences.english: Many AI algorithms are trained on enormous quantities of data.

relatedExpressions.meaning: recommendation algorithm — used by streaming and social media platforms
algorithmic bias — when an algorithm produces systematically skewed results
algorithm training — the process of training an AI model

grammarNotes: Dati is the plural of dato (masculine noun: il dato, i dati). In technology and everyday digital contexts it is almost always used in the plural — 'i dati' — because data in Italian, as in technical English, is treated as a plural concept. The singular dato exists and means a single piece of data, a fact, or a datum, but you'll encounter it far less frequently than the plural. Key compound phrases: 'dati personali' (personal data), 'protezione dei dati' (data protection), 'raccolta dati' (data collection), 'analisi dei dati' (data analysis).
learnerNotes: Dati is one of those words that sounds simple but appears constantly in Italian digital life — cookie notices, app permissions, privacy policies, news articles. Every time you download an Italian app or visit an Italian website, you'll encounter 'i tuoi dati personali' (your personal data) and 'trattamento dei dati' (data processing). The GDPR — known in Italy as GDPR or Regolamento Generale sulla Protezione dei Dati — has made data privacy vocabulary part of everyday Italian literacy. Knowing dati and its compounds unlocks a whole register of contemporary Italian that learners often find opaque.

exampleSentences.italian: Questa app raccoglie i tuoi dati personali.
exampleSentences.english: This app collects your personal data.

exampleSentences.italian: I dati mostrano un aumento significativo degli utenti.
exampleSentences.english: The data shows a significant increase in users.

exampleSentences.italian: La protezione dei dati è un diritto fondamentale in Europa.
exampleSentences.english: Data protection is a fundamental right in Europe.

exampleSentences.italian: Bisogna analizzare i dati prima di trarre conclusioni.
exampleSentences.english: You need to analyse the data before drawing conclusions.

exampleSentences.italian: Non condividere mai i tuoi dati bancari online.
exampleSentences.english: Never share your banking data online.

relatedExpressions.meaning: personal data — the key term in privacy law and app permissions
data protection — central concept in GDPR and Italian law
a fact / a matter of fact — the singular used idiomatically

grammarNotes: Modello is a masculine noun (il modello, i modelli). In Italian it has a wide range of meanings — a fashion model (il modello / la modella), a model car, a template or form, a role model — and in technology it has taken on the AI sense of a trained computational system. In the tech register you'll encounter 'modello linguistico' (language model), 'modello di IA' (AI model), and 'grande modello linguistico' (large language model / LLM). The gender of modello stays masculine regardless of context; the fashion/human sense has a feminine form modella for women.
learnerNotes: In contemporary Italian tech journalism, modello has become the standard translation for the English 'model' in AI contexts. You'll read 'il modello è stato addestrato su miliardi di parametri' (the model was trained on billions of parameters) and 'quale modello usi?' (which model do you use?) in casual AI conversation. The potential for confusion with other meanings of modello is real — context usually resolves it, but pay attention. A useful phrase to know: 'modello di riferimento' (reference model / benchmark) appears in both tech and business Italian.

exampleSentences.italian: Questo è un modello linguistico addestrato su enormi quantità di testo.
exampleSentences.english: This is a language model trained on enormous quantities of text.

exampleSentences.italian: Quale modello di IA usi per il tuo lavoro?
exampleSentences.english: Which AI model do you use for your work?

exampleSentences.italian: I grandi modelli linguistici stanno rivoluzionando molti settori.
exampleSentences.english: Large language models are revolutionising many sectors.

exampleSentences.italian: Il modello ha fatto un errore nella traduzione.
exampleSentences.english: The model made an error in the translation.

relatedExpressions.meaning: language model — the Italian term for LLM
large language model (LLM) — the full Italian term
reference model / benchmark — used in tech and business contexts

grammarNotes: Apprendimento automatico is a masculine noun phrase (l'apprendimento automatico). Apprendimento means learning or acquisition (from the verb apprendere, to learn), and automatico means automatic — together they render the English 'machine learning' precisely. In formal and academic Italian this is the standard term; in practice, many Italian tech professionals simply say 'machine learning' using the English term directly, especially in startup and tech-company environments. Both forms are correct and widely understood; the Italian term is preferred in journalism, government documents, and educational contexts.
learnerNotes: Italian tech vocabulary presents an interesting split: some English terms are adopted wholesale (like 'machine learning', 'startup', 'software'), while others have established Italian equivalents that are genuinely used. Apprendimento automatico is in the second category — it's a real, living Italian term, not just a translation exercise. A related term worth knowing is 'apprendimento profondo' (deep learning), which follows the same pattern. If you're reading Italian AI news, you'll encounter both the Italian and English forms, sometimes in the same article — Italian tech writers often use both interchangeably.

exampleSentences.italian: L'apprendimento automatico permette ai computer di imparare dai dati.
exampleSentences.english: Machine learning allows computers to learn from data.

exampleSentences.italian: Molte aziende usano l'apprendimento automatico per analizzare i clienti.
exampleSentences.english: Many companies use machine learning to analyse customers.

exampleSentences.italian: Il corso universitario copre sia l'IA che l'apprendimento automatico.
exampleSentences.english: The university course covers both AI and machine learning.

exampleSentences.italian: L'apprendimento automatico è alla base dei sistemi di raccomandazione.
exampleSentences.english: Machine learning is at the foundation of recommendation systems.

relatedExpressions.meaning: deep learning — a subset of machine learning using neural networks
neural network — the computational architecture behind deep learning
model training — the process of teaching a model from data

grammarNotes: Dispositivo is a masculine noun (il dispositivo, i dispositivi). It is the standard Italian word for any electronic or digital device — smartphone, tablet, computer, smart speaker, wearable — and appears constantly in app settings, tech support, and everyday conversation. The plural i dispositivi is frequently used: 'tutti i tuoi dispositivi' (all your devices) is a phrase you'll encounter in cloud storage settings, email clients, and security notifications. It can also refer to non-digital devices or mechanisms in formal/technical contexts, but the digital sense dominates contemporary usage.
learnerNotes: Dispositivo is one of the most useful technology words to internalize because it appears in so many practical contexts — phone settings menus, Wi-Fi setup screens, app permissions, security alerts. When your Italian phone says 'dispositivo non riconosciuto' it means 'unrecognised device'; 'gestisci i tuoi dispositivi' means 'manage your devices.' The word feels formal but is completely standard across all registers in tech contexts — there is no more casual alternative. Learners sometimes reach for the English 'device' in conversation, but dispositivo is short enough and natural enough that it's worth using.

exampleSentences.italian: Questo dispositivo non è compatibile con l'ultima versione del sistema.
exampleSentences.english: This device is not compatible with the latest version of the system.

exampleSentences.italian: Puoi accedere al tuo account da qualsiasi dispositivo.
exampleSentences.english: You can access your account from any device.

exampleSentences.italian: Il dispositivo si è spento improvvisamente senza motivo.
exampleSentences.english: The device switched off suddenly for no reason.

exampleSentences.italian: Connetti il dispositivo alla rete Wi-Fi per continuare.
exampleSentences.english: Connect the device to the Wi-Fi network to continue.

exampleSentences.italian: I dispositivi indossabili raccolgono dati sulla salute in tempo reale.
exampleSentences.english: Wearable devices collect health data in real time.

relatedExpressions.meaning: mobile device — smartphone or tablet
wearable device — smartwatch, fitness tracker, etc.
device management — common in IT and cloud account settings

grammarNotes: Piattaforma is a feminine noun (la piattaforma, le piattaforme). Its literal meaning is a physical platform or stage, but in contemporary Italian the digital sense dominates in everyday conversation: social media platforms, streaming platforms, e-commerce platforms. The plural le piattaforme is widely used: 'le piattaforme di streaming' (streaming platforms), 'le grandi piattaforme tecnologiche' (big tech platforms). It is often used with the definite article even in generic statements: 'la piattaforma è andata offline' (the platform went offline).
learnerNotes: Piattaforma is one of those words that has been so thoroughly absorbed into the digital vocabulary that Italians use it constantly without thinking of its physical origin. It appears in news coverage of tech regulation ('le piattaforme devono rispettare le norme europee'), in everyday conversation ('su quale piattaforma guardi i film?'), and in political debate about digital power. A useful distinction: Italians often specify the type — 'piattaforma social' (social media platform), 'piattaforma di streaming' (streaming platform), 'piattaforma di e-commerce' — rather than just saying 'piattaforma' alone, which can be ambiguous.

exampleSentences.italian: Su quale piattaforma guardi le serie televisive?
exampleSentences.english: Which platform do you watch TV series on?

exampleSentences.italian: Le grandi piattaforme tecnologiche sono sempre più regolamentate.
exampleSentences.english: Big tech platforms are increasingly regulated.

exampleSentences.italian: La piattaforma è andata offline per manutenzione.
exampleSentences.english: The platform went offline for maintenance.

exampleSentences.italian: Molti creator guadagnano pubblicando contenuti sulle piattaforme social.
exampleSentences.english: Many creators earn money by publishing content on social platforms.

relatedExpressions.meaning: streaming platform — Netflix, Disney+, RaiPlay, etc.
social media platform
digital platform — the broadest term covering all online services

grammarNotes: Aggiornamento is a masculine noun (l'aggiornamento, gli aggiornamenti), derived from the verb aggiornare (to update, to bring up to date — literally 'to bring to today', from giorno, day). In digital contexts it is the standard word for a software or system update. The verb form aggiornare is equally important and widely used: 'aggiornare il sistema' (to update the system), 'aggiornare un'app' (to update an app). The reflexive aggiornarsi means to keep oneself informed or up to date on a topic — a useful figurative extension.
learnerNotes: Every Italian smartphone user sees aggiornamento constantly — it is the word iOS and Android both use for 'update' in their Italian interfaces. 'Aggiornamento disponibile' (update available), 'installa l'aggiornamento' (install the update), 'aggiornamento in corso' (update in progress) — these are phrases you'll encounter daily. Beyond the tech sense, aggiornarsi is a valuable verb for conversations about keeping up with news or developments: 'devo aggiornarmi sulla situazione' (I need to catch up on the situation) is completely natural Italian. The word has a satisfying elegance — it literally means 'bringing something to today.'

exampleSentences.italian: C'è un aggiornamento disponibile per il tuo telefono.
exampleSentences.english: There is an update available for your phone.

exampleSentences.italian: L'aggiornamento del sistema operativo ha risolto il problema.
exampleSentences.english: The operating system update fixed the problem.

exampleSentences.italian: Devo aggiornare tutte le app prima di partire.
exampleSentences.english: I need to update all the apps before I leave.

exampleSentences.italian: Mi sono aggiornato sulle ultime notizie sull'IA.
exampleSentences.english: I caught up on the latest news about AI.

exampleSentences.italian: L'aggiornamento automatico è attivato per impostazione predefinita.
exampleSentences.english: Automatic update is activated by default.

relatedExpressions.meaning: automatic update — a common setting in phone and app management
to update oneself / to keep up to date — used both literally and figuratively
security update — a software patch addressing vulnerabilities

englishTranslation: to process / to elaborate / to develop
grammarNotes: Elaborare is a regular -are verb and conjugates predictably: elaboro, elabori, elabora, elaboriamo, elaborate, elaborano. In compound tenses it takes avere: ho elaborato, aveva elaborato. In technology it means to process — 'elaborare i dati' (to process data), 'elaborare un'immagine' (to process an image). Beyond tech, it carries the broader sense of working something through carefully: elaborare un'idea (to develop an idea), elaborare un piano (to work out a plan), elaborare un lutto (to process grief). This range of meaning makes it a versatile and valuable verb.
learnerNotes: Elaborare sits at the intersection of technology and general intellectual vocabulary, which makes it doubly useful. In tech contexts it is the standard verb for computational processing — if a computer or AI system is doing something with data, it is elaborating it. In everyday Italian it appears in discussions of ideas, plans, and emotions: 'ho bisogno di tempo per elaborare quello che è successo' (I need time to process what happened) is completely natural. The noun elaborazione (processing, elaboration) follows the same pattern and is equally common — 'elaborazione dei dati' (data processing) is a phrase you'll see on Italian cookie notices and privacy policies.

exampleSentences.italian: Il processore elabora milioni di operazioni al secondo.
exampleSentences.english: The processor handles millions of operations per second.

exampleSentences.italian: L'IA elabora le immagini in pochi millisecondi.
exampleSentences.english: The AI processes the images in a few milliseconds.

exampleSentences.italian: Abbiamo bisogno di tempo per elaborare una strategia efficace.
exampleSentences.english: We need time to work out an effective strategy.

exampleSentences.italian: Ha impiegato mesi per elaborare il trauma della perdita.
exampleSentences.english: It took him months to process the trauma of the loss.

relatedExpressions.meaning: data processing — standard term in tech and privacy contexts
natural language processing (NLP) — a key field in AI
to work out / develop a plan — common in business and strategy

englishTranslation: to share / to share online / to share an opinion
grammarNotes: Condividere is an irregular -ere verb. Its past participle is condiviso (irregular — not condividuto), and it takes avere in compound tenses: ho condiviso, aveva condiviso. Present tense: condivido, condividi, condivide, condividiamo, condividete, condividono. In digital contexts it is the standard translation of 'to share' — condividere un post, condividere un link, condividere una foto. It also carries the non-digital sense of sharing or holding a view in common: 'condivido la tua opinione' (I share your opinion). The noun form is condivisione (sharing).
learnerNotes: Condividere is the verb behind the ubiquitous 'condividi' button on every Italian social media interface — the Italian equivalent of 'Share.' It has two distinct but related uses that learners need to keep clear: the digital sense (to post/forward/share content online) and the intellectual sense (to hold or share a view, experience, or value in common). 'Condivido quello che hai detto' does not mean 'I shared what you said online' — it means 'I agree with what you said / I share your view.' Context almost always makes it clear, but the double meaning is worth internalising. The irregular past participle condiviso (not condividuto) is the most common error.

exampleSentences.italian: Ha condiviso il video sui suoi profili social.
exampleSentences.english: She shared the video on her social profiles.

exampleSentences.italian: Puoi condividere questo documento con il tuo team.
exampleSentences.english: You can share this document with your team.

exampleSentences.italian: Condivido pienamente la tua preoccupazione.
exampleSentences.english: I fully share your concern.

exampleSentences.italian: Non condividere mai la tua password con nessuno.
exampleSentences.english: Never share your password with anyone.

exampleSentences.italian: Il post è stato condiviso migliaia di volte in poche ore.
exampleSentences.english: The post was shared thousands of times in a few hours.

relatedExpressions.meaning: sharing — the noun form, used both digitally and figuratively
share — the imperative/button label on social media interfaces
to share / hold an opinion — to agree with someone's view

grammarNotes: Interfaccia is a feminine noun (l'interfaccia, le interfacce). Despite ending in -a, it follows the standard feminine pattern with -e in the plural — le interfacce, not le interfaccie. This is a common stumbling block for learners. In tech contexts you'll encounter 'interfaccia utente' (user interface / UI), 'interfaccia grafica' (graphical interface / GUI), and 'interfaccia intuitiva' (intuitive interface). The word can also be used metaphorically to describe a point of contact between two systems, organisations, or people, though this figurative use is less common.
learnerNotes: Interfaccia is one of the Italian tech words that looks and sounds very close to its English equivalent — which makes it easy to learn but also means the plural trips people up. Remember: le interfacce (not le interfaccie). In practice, Italians in tech contexts often mix Italian and English freely — 'l'UI è molto pulita' or 'l'interfaccia è molto pulita' are both natural. However, reading Italian tech reviews, app descriptions, and software documentation, you'll find interfaccia is the consistently preferred Italian term. 'Interfaccia utente' is the full standard phrase for 'user interface'; in speech it's often shortened to just 'l'interfaccia'.

exampleSentences.italian: L'interfaccia di questa app è molto intuitiva.
exampleSentences.english: This app's interface is very intuitive.

exampleSentences.italian: Hanno aggiornato l'interfaccia utente nella nuova versione.
exampleSentences.english: They updated the user interface in the new version.

exampleSentences.italian: L'interfaccia grafica permette di usare il programma senza conoscere i comandi.
exampleSentences.english: The graphical interface lets you use the programme without knowing the commands.

exampleSentences.italian: La nuova interfaccia è molto più semplice da usare.
exampleSentences.english: The new interface is much easier to use.

relatedExpressions.meaning: user interface (UI) — the standard Italian term
graphical user interface (GUI)
user experience (UX) — the broader design concept
